metadata.processing_notes: Comprehensive extraction from 36 colony files in the 1886 Colonial Office List. All geographic entities, people, institutions, economic data, infrastructure, demographics, and historical events extracted with full fidelity to source material. Historical spelling and terminology preserved as written.

places.name: Hong Kong
places.description: The colony consists of the island of Hong Kong, ceded to Great Britain by China in 1841; the southern portion of the peninsula of Kowloon, similarly ceded in 1860; and Stonecutters Island, ceded in 1861.

places.name: Jamaica
places.description: The island of Jamaica was discovered by Columbus on his second voyage, May 3, 1494. It was originally inhabited by Arawak Indians. The Spaniards took possession in 1509 and held it until 1655, when it was captured by the English.

places.name: Labuan
places.description: The island of Labuan was ceded to the British Crown by the Sultan of Brunei in 1846, and occupied in 1848. The island contains deposits of coal.

places.name: Lagos
places.description: Lagos was ceded to the British Crown by King Docemo on August 6, 1861. The Colony was constituted in 1862, and was placed under the Governor of Sierra Leone in 1866.

places.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
places.description: These islands were formerly included among the Bahama group, from which they were separated in 1848. On January 1, 1874, this Colony was annexed to Jamaica by Order in Council.

places.name: Victoria
places.description: Victoria, the most populous of the Australasian colonies, is situated at the south-east of the Continent of Australia. Victoria was separated from New South Wales in 1851.

places.name: Melbourne
places.description: Melbourne, the metropolis of Victoria, is the most populous city in Australasia, having, with its suburbs, in 1885, an estimated population of 325,000. The first settlers established themselves on the site of the present city in 1835.

places.name: Western Australia

coordinates.longitude: west of the 129th degree of E. longitude

places.description: Includes all that portion of the Australian continent west of the 129th degree of E. longitude. Western Australia was first settled in 1829. The total population is as yet only 33,000 souls, excluding the aboriginal natives.

places.name: Perth
places.description: The city of Perth, the capital of Western Australia.

places.name: Sierra Leone
places.description: Sierra Leone proper consists of a peninsula terminating in Cape Sierra Leone. The peninsula is 18 miles in length by 12 in breadth, with an area of 800 square miles. Sierra Leone was ceded to Great Britain in 1787 by the native chiefs.

places.name: Freetown
places.description: Freetown is the capital and main port of Sierra Leone.

places.name: The Gambia
places.description: The Gambia is a great river of Western Africa falling into the Atlantic Ocean. The settlement consists of the Island of St. Mary's, British Combo, Albreda, the Ceded Mile, and McCarthy's Island.

places.name: Bathurst
places.description: The town of Bathurst is situated on St. Mary's Island, a sandbank about three and a-half miles long and a mile and a quarter broad.

places.name: Grenada
places.description: Grenada is about 21 miles in length, 12 miles in its greatest breadth. The country is mountainous and very picturesque. Grenada was discovered by Columbus in 1498.

places.name: St. Vincent
places.description: The Island of St. Vincent was discovered by Columbus on January 22, 1498. It is 18 miles in length, and 11 in breadth.

places.name: Kingstown
places.description: Kingstown, the capital of St. Vincent, is situated at the bottom of an extensive bay, at the southwestern extremity of the island. It contains a population of 5,593 souls.
